name: Sky Tower
bio: A 328-metre tower with observation decks, a glass floor and a SkyWalk, the tallest structure in the Southern Hemisphere.

name: Rangitoto Island
bio: A symmetrical volcanic island in the Hauraki Gulf, with a 253-metre summit walk through lava fields and pōhutukawa forest.

name: Auckland War Memorial Museum
bio: A neoclassical museum of Māori and Pacific treasures, natural history and war memorials, set in the Auckland Domain.

name: Piha
bio: A wild black-sand surf beach beneath the dramatic Lion Rock, on the Waitākere coast.

name: Mount Eden
bio: The highest volcanic cone on the isthmus, with a grassy crater and the best panorama over the city.

name: Viaduct Harbour
bio: A waterfront district of restaurants and bars around a marina of yachts used in America's Cup racing.

name: Auckland Art Gallery
bio: New Zealand's largest art collection, from colonial works and Māori portraiture to contemporary art, in a heritage building.

name: Devonport
bio: A village of Victorian villas and cafés reached by a 12-minute ferry, with Mount Victoria's harbour views.

name: Kelly Tarlton's Sea Life Aquarium
bio: An aquarium with an underwater tunnel through sharks and rays, and a colony of king and gentoo penguins.

name: Muriwai
bio: A black-sand surf beach with a clifftop colony of thousands of nesting gannets from August to March.

name: Karekare
bio: A secluded black-sand beach with waterfalls nearby, used as a location in the film The Piano.

name: Karangahape Road
bio: Auckland's creative street, lined with vintage shops, bars, galleries and street art.

name: MOTAT
bio: A transport and technology museum in Western Springs, with a vintage tramway and collections of aircraft, trams and trains.

name: Mission Bay
bio: A sheltered sandy beach on Tāmaki Drive, backed by cafés and ice-cream shops, an easy ferry-and-walk from the city.

name: Auckland Zoo
bio: A conservation-focused zoo beside Western Springs Park, with kiwi and other native wildlife and animals from abroad.

name: Auckland Domain
bio: The city's oldest park, 75 hectares of lawns and volcanic crater around the Wintergardens and Auckland Museum.

name: One Tree Hill
bio: A 182-metre volcanic peak and ancestral maunga rising out of Cornwall Park, with views over the city and both harbours.

name: Parnell
bio: Auckland's oldest suburb, a hillside of heritage buildings, galleries and cafés, with the Parnell Rose Gardens above the harbour.

name: Ponsonby
bio: A villa-lined ridge two kilometres from the CBD, famous for the cafés, restaurants and boutiques along Ponsonby Road.

name: Takapuna Beach
bio: A wide sandy North Shore beach looking out to Rangitoto Island, with cafés and shops a short walk behind it.

name: Wynyard Quarter
bio: A reclaimed waterfront strip of restaurants, parks and working wharves beside the Viaduct, home to the Auckland Fish Market.

name: North Head
bio: A volcanic headland above Devonport with Māori terraces, a maze of military tunnels and views across the harbour to the city.

name: Onetangi
bio: Waiheke's longest beach, a sweep of white sand with cafés and a surf-life-saving club.

name: Cable Bay Vineyards
bio: A hillside winery with a restaurant and tasting room looking over the Hauraki Gulf and the Auckland skyline.

name: Oneroa
bio: The island's main village, with cafés, galleries and a sheltered beach beside a clifftop walk.

name: Stony Batter Historic Reserve
bio: Second World War coastal-defence tunnels and gun emplacements on a farm at the island's eastern end.

name: Matiatia
bio: Waiheke's ferry wharf and bay, with a walkway up to headland views over Auckland.

name: Aotea Track
bio: A multi-day track across the island's rugged interior, past hot springs, kauri forest and high ridgelines.

name: Kaitoke Hot Springs
bio: Natural geothermal pools in the bush, reached by a short boardwalk walk from the road.

name: Medlands Beach
bio: A long white-sand surf beach on the east coast with views of the offshore islands.

name: Windy Canyon
bio: A short walk through a narrow volcanic gorge to a ridge with wide views of the island.

name: Cape Rodney-Okakari Point Marine Reserve
bio: New Zealand's first marine reserve, known as Goat Island, with snorkelling among large snapper and crayfish.

name: Kawau Island
bio: A gulf island with historic Mansion House, wallabies and boat-only beaches, reached by ferry from Sandspit.

name: Tawharanui Regional Park
bio: A coastal park and open sanctuary with surf beaches, walking tracks and native birds such as takahē and kiwi.

name: Omaha
bio: A long white-sand beach at the end of a sandspit, with calm swimming and views to the offshore islands.
